Project definition is the first step of the cyberrisk management process.

This preparation step allows the cyberrisk manager to define what will be assessed, identify the people that will participate, and document important context.

It is a best practice to group resources together under the same project when there are similarities between them that would make it most efficient to manage their security under a single security plan. When doing this grouping for your project, consider the following attributes of the resources:

  1. Function or Purpose
  2. Criticality
  3. Target or Current Data Classification
  4. Ownership

Control assessment is the second step of the cyberrisk management process.

During this step, potential vulnerabilities in your security practices are identified.

Security controls that benefit the resources included in the scope of your project are often implemented and controlled elsewhere in the organization. These are known as common controls because they are common across many parts of the organization. You may optionally select to inherit information about common controls from various groups who have opted to share this information with consumers of their services.

Risk Analysis is the third step of the cyberrisk management process.

Risk is a measure of the extent to which an entity is threatened by a potential circumstance or event and is typically a function of the adverse impacts that would arise if the circumstance or event occurs and the likelihood of occurrence. Information security risks are those risks that arise from the loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability of information or information systems and reflect the potential adverse impacts to organizational operations and assets, individuals, or other associated entities.

The objective of the Risk Analysis step of Risk Management is to produce a register of the risks that will be managed.

The risk recommendations provided below are based on three components:

  1. Business impacts identified in the define step of the risk management cycle,
  2. Responses to questions you answered in the assess step, and
  3. Quantitative assessment of threat prevalence and frequency as interpreted by the SibylSoft Threat Assessment Team.
This information is combined to create risk statements with ratings as to the severity of each risk. If you haven't already done so, you can complete the business impact assessment on step one and ensure you've identified all implemented controls in step two to get the best possible recommendations from Sibylity.

Security planning is the fourth and final step of the cyberrisk management process.

During this planning and approval step, risk treatment decisions are considered and selected for each risk statement added during risk analysis. Proposed risk treatment decisions should be reviewed with risk owners to ensure they are consistent with risk tolerance goals.

The end objective of the Security Planning step of Risk Management is to produce an approved information security plan.

Risk Treatment

Select the treatment that you reccommend for each risk that was added to the Risk Register in step 3.

Rating Risk Statement
89 Risk of reduction in student enrollment from misuse of resources due to the absence of a determination, using the university Data Classification Standard, of which data classifications will be supported by relevant systems and/or devices
Risk Transfer Examples:
  • Purchase cybersecurity insurance.
  • Pursue legal options (e.g., business associate agreement (BAA)).
  • Transfer risk to a vendor or service provider, ensuring the party can handle the risk.
Risk Avoidance Examples:
  • Change project scope.
  • Change project objectives.
  • Clarify requirements to eliminate ambiguities and misunderstandings.
  • Gain expertise to remove information security risks.
Risk Acceptance Examples:
  • The value to the business of accepting the risk outweighs the potential impact of the risk.
  • The acceptance of risk is a strategy like any other and should be documented and communicated.
  • Risk acceptance can be passive. In this case, the consequences are dealt with after the risk is realized.

Risk Mitigation: Technical, administrative, and physical controls implemented to reduce likelihood and/orminimize impact. Select from suggested mitigations or add your own.

Privacy Policy

SibylSoft Privacy Policy

Overview

SibylSoft, Inc. (“we” or “us” or “our”) is serious about protecting the privacy of its clients and their Authorized Users.  Under this SibylSoft Privacy Policy (this “Privacy Policy”), “you” or “your” refers to the entity with which we have entered into a Subscription Agreement (as defined in our Terms and Conditions of Use  the “Terms of Use”) as well as your Authorized Users as applicable.  We understand your concerns regarding how information about you is used and shared, and we appreciate your trust that we will do so carefully and sensibly.  This Privacy Policy describes what information we collect about you from your use of the Site (as defined below), how we collect it, how we use it, with whom we may share it, and what choices you have regarding it.  This Privacy Policy does not pertain to, or govern, our collection, use, storage, or protection of any personal information you submit to us via any other means, including, but not limited to, by phone, e-mail other than through use of the Site, or the United States Postal Service.  This Privacy Policy is incorporated into and is a part of the Terms of Use of our site (www.SibylSoft.com, www.Sibylity.com, or any related or replacement site, the “Site”).  We encourage you to become familiar with the terms and conditions of both this Privacy Policy and the Terms of Use.  Capitalized Terms used, but not otherwise defined herein have the meanings given to such terms in the Terms of Use.


BY ACCESSING AND USING THE SITE, YOU AGREE THAT YOU HAVE READ AND UNDERSTAND THIS PRIVACY POLICY AND YOU ACCEPT AND CONSENT TO THE PRIVACY PRACTICES (AND ANY USES AND DISCLOSURES OF INFORMATION ABOUT YOU) THAT ARE DESCRIBED IN THIS PRIVACY POLICY.


Changes to Privacy Policy

Due to changes in relevant and applicable legal or regulatory requirements, our business practices; or in our attempt to better serve your needs, we may change our privacy practices and this Notice of Website Practices.  Notice of such changes to our privacy practices will be given in the manner described in the Terms of Use and a revised Privacy Policy will be posted on the Site.


What Information Do We Collect?

We may collect certain identifying information from or about you in connection with your use of the Site.  For example, we may retain the content of, and metadata regarding, any correspondence you may have with us or our representatives, regardless of the subject matter or the mode of communication by which such correspondence is made.  This information helps us to improve our products and services, as well as the Site and the content, materials, opportunities, and services that we feature or describe on the Site, and to more effectively and efficiently respond to both current and future inquiries.


Certain information on our Site is collected automatically by means of various software tools.  We have a legitimate interest in using such information to assist in log-in, systems administration purposes, information security and abuse prevention, to track user trends, and to analyze the effectiveness of our Online Services.  Alone or in combination with other information, such automatically collected information may constitute personal data.


Certain aspects of the Site may allow you to voluntarily submit information to us.  For example, providing personally identifiable information for the purpose of Site support is a voluntary submission of information under applicable law.  We may use and keep the information that you submit on file as necessary and appropriate for the purposes for which it was submitted.  You should be mindful of the information that you choose to submit to us and make sure that this information is complete and accurate.


As with many other websites, the web servers used to operate the Site may collect certain data pertaining to you and the equipment and communications method that you use to access the Internet and the Site.  Without combining these data with other sources of information, they do not readily or personally identify you.  They may reveal such things as the Internet protocol (“IP”) address assigned to your computer, specific pages that you accessed on the Site or immediately prior to visiting the Site, and the length of time you spend in a visit to the Site.  The purposes for which this information is collected and used include facilitating Site operation and system administration, generating aggregate, non-identifiable statistical information, monitoring and analyzing Site traffic and usage patterns, and improving the content and content delivery with regard to the Site and the content, materials, opportunities, and services that we describe or make available on the Site.


We may also use “cookies” (that is, small text files stored on your computer) to help track and customize your access and use of the Site.  Cookies store and retain information that helps us recognize you when you return to the Site following a previous visit.  Most popular Internet browser packages allow you to configure the browser so as not to accept cookies.  However, setting your browser to reject cookies may, in certain instances, prevent you from taking full advantage of the Site and the materials, products, and services that we make available on the Site.


Authorized Users may also provide certain User Content in connection with the services that we provide.  We may de-identify and aggregate such User Content for our internal use including, but not limited to improve our services, content, user interface and Online Services.


How Do We Use The Information That We Collect?

In addition to the uses mentioned or described above, or otherwise described in our Terms of Use, we may use the information that we collect from or about you to analyze and improve the content, features, materials, and opportunities that we make available on the Site, to notify you of changes made to the Site or new opportunities made available on or through the Site, to evaluate your needs and customize the Site content delivered to you according to those needs, to send you promotional materials that you request from us, and for other legitimate and lawful business purposes.  If you contact us for support or assistance in connection with using the Site, we may use information about you or your system for purposes such as verifying whether your system meets the minimum requirements needed to use the Site and our various services.


With Whom Do We Share Information That We Collect?

In addition to the uses mentioned or described above or otherwise described in our Terms of Use, in the course of conducting our business, we may transfer the information that we collect or that you submit to us, whether solicited or unsolicited, among our various offices and to the trusted business and marketing partners and service providers that we utilize in operating, maintaining, and further developing the Site and in delivering the content, materials, and opportunities that we make available on or through the Site.  The sharing of such information is only to the extent necessary and appropriate, including, for example, for purposes of communicating with you or fulfilling your requests for Site content and materials.  We may also produce reports on Site traffic or usage patterns and share these reports with our business partners and others, but the information contained in these reports is anonymous and does not allow identification of any specific individual.  Please rest assured that, other than as expressly provided in this Privacy Policy, any personal information that we obtain about you through the Site will be reported outside our organization only in de-identified, aggregated formats that do not identify any particular individual or company.


We may disclose information about you if we become subject to a subpoena or court order or if we are otherwise legally required to disclose such information.  We may also use and disclose information about you to establish or exercise our legal rights, to enforce the Terms of Use, to assert and defend against legal claims, or if we believe such disclosure is necessary to investigate, prevent, or take other action regarding actual or suspected illegal or fraudulent activities or potential threats to the physical safety or well-being of any person.


It is possible that the structure of our business might change or that it might merge or otherwise combine with, or that it or portions of our business might be acquired by, another company.  In any such transactions, customer information generally is, will most probably be, and should be expected to be one of the transferred business assets.


What Choices Do You Have?

In general, in order to use any functionality of the Site, you must login using your unique email address and password, which we track to unsure only Authorized Users are accessing the Site.  We may track the internet address of the domains from which users visit the Site and analyze this data for trends and statistics, but, in such an event, the individual user, in most cases, remains anonymous.  The information collected and analyzed is used to improve our products and services.  If you provide information to us through the Site, that information will be used in the normal course of our business to provide services to you or on your behalf.  The information will be shared only as described in the Terms of Use and this Privacy Policy.  If you choose not to provide information through the Site you may not be able to use certain functions, or maximize the benefits, of the Site including those for which you have subscribed.


When corresponding with us or our representatives, or when making a request for information, submitting information, or otherwise interacting with us or others through the Site, you choose what information to supply, what questions to pose and comments to make, whether you wish to receive further information, and by what method of communication that information should be delivered to you.  Please take care to share only such information as is needed or that you believe is appropriate.


How Do We Protect Information Collected About You?

We take commercially reasonable measures to secure and protect information transmitted via or stored on the Site.  However, we cannot and do not guarantee that any such transmissions or information will be totally secure.  Unencrypted Internet communications are not secure, and no security measures are impenetrable.  You agree to immediately notify us of any breach, or suspected breach, of Site security, this Privacy Policy, or the Terms of Use of which you become aware.


Cookies
Cookies are small text files that are placed on your computer by websites that you visit.  Cookies are widely used in order to make websites and applications work, or work more efficiently, and help such websites and applications remember certain information about you, either for the duration of your visit (using a “session” cookie) or for repeat visits (using a “persistent” cookie).


As detailed in this Privacy Policy, our use of cookies may involve the collection and use of your information, such as IP addresses, or other online mobile identifiers.  The cookies used on this website are as follows:


  1. Strictly necessary cookies:  These are cookies that are required for the operation of our websites and cannot be switched off in our systems.  They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in, or filling in forms.  You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the Service will not then work.  These cookies do not store any personal data.
  2. Functionality cookies:  These are used to recognize you when you return to our websites.  This enables us to personalize our content for you and remember your preferences (e.g., your choice of language or region).
  3. Performance/Analytical cookies:  These allow us to recognize and count the number of website visitors and to see how visitors move around our websites when they are using them.  This helps us to improve the way our websites work, for example, by ensuring that users are finding what they are looking for easily.  All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous.  If you do not allow these cookies, we will not know when you have visited our site and will not be able to monitor its performance.
  4. Targeting cookies:  These cookies record your visit to our websites, the pages you have visited and the links you have followed.  We will use this information to make our websites and the advertising displayed on it more relevant to your interests.  We may also share this information with third parties for this purpose. 
  5. Third Party and Social Media Cookies:
  6. Flash Cookies:
  7. Tracking Technologies Including Pixels, Script, Web Beacons/Gifs, Page Tags:
  8. Tracking Via Mobile Apps:


If you access the service through a subscription agreement or other contract administered by your organization, cookies may be placed in accordance with the contract with your organization.


Linked Sites
For your convenience, some hyperlinks may be posted on the Site that link to other websites not under our control.  We are not responsible for, and this Privacy Policy does not apply to, the privacy practices of those websites or of any companies that we do not own or control.  We encourage you to seek out and read the privacy policy of each website that you visit.  In addition, should you happen to initiate a transaction on a website that our Site links to, even if you reached that website through our Site, the information that you submit to complete that transaction becomes subject to the privacy practices of the operator of that linked website. You should read that website’s privacy policies to understand how personal information that is collected about you is used and protected.


Whom Can You Contact For More Information?

If you have any questions or suggestions about us, the Site, or our products, services, or privacy practices, please contact us feedback@sibylsoft.com.

    1. Introduction

    Security plans provide a summary of the security requirements for an information resource and describe the security controls in place or planned for meeting those requirements. Security planning is an important activity that supports and enables greater assurance of secure operations and should be repeated and refreshed as system events trigger the need for revision in order to accurately reflect the most current state of the system.

    5. Resource Classification

    FIPS 199 is the standard used by all federal agencies to categorize information and information systems collected or maintained by or on behalf of each agency based on the objectives of providing appropriate levels of information security according to impact. Security categorization standards for information and information systems provide a common framework and understanding for expressing security that promotes effective management and oversight of information security programs and consistent reporting on the adequacy and effectiveness of information security policies, procedures, and practices.

    Expression

    SCHuman Resources Process and Data = {(confidentiality, Low), (integrity, Medium), (availability, High)}


    5.1 Information Types

    The following tables identify the information types that are input, stored, processed, and/or output from the resource. The selection of the information types is based on guidance provided by NIST SP 800-60, Guide for Mapping Types of Information and Information Systems to Security Categories and FIPS Pub 199, Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information Systems.

    The tables also identify the security impact levels for confidentiality, integrity, and availability for each of the information types expressed as low, moderate, or high. The security impact levels are based on the potential impact definitions for each of the security objectives (i.e., confidentiality, integrity, and availability) discussed in NIST SP 800-60 and FIPS Pub 199.

    In any instances where the owner has chosen to deviate from the NIST recommended impact level, complete justification has been provided.

    6. Business Impact Assessment

    In recognition of the opportunity dimension of risk, an assessment of potential impacts supplements the data type assessment and provides additional insight into the relationship between the organization and the managed risks. These insights have guided the risk handling determinations and may serve as full or partial justification for any risk acceptance.

    Impact Type Level of Concern Comments
    Lost sales and/or income Very (3) —
    Delayed sale and/or income Extreme (4) —
    Reduction in enrollment Moderate (2) —
    Loss of research opportunities Very (3) —
    Missed revenue opportunities Extreme (4) —
    Loss of existing awards None (0) —
